page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-1 is an entry-level general-purpose instance providing dedicated computing resources for baseline cloud operations. The virtual machine runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The instance configuration exposes 1 physical core mapped to 1 vCPU with 1 thread per core. Memory is provisioned at 3.75 GB per core, maintaining a standard general-purpose compute-to-memory ratio. The cache hierarchy includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and access to 45 MB of L3 cache. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AES, FMA, and BMI2, while omitting newer vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX.

From a system architecture perspective, the n1-standard-1 instance includes no bundled local storage and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring attached persistent network storage. Benchmark evaluations reflect modest throughput across compute and memory operations due to its single-thread constraint. Both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests measure at 1088.79, while Geekbench records 895.0 for single-core and 898.0 for multi-core performance. Memory bandwidth benchmarks yield 10.68 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 9.71 GB/sec for writes. The instance supports 1.29 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.21 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

The single-core ceiling and modest memory footprint create trade-offs between predictable execution and throughput scale. Dedicated CPU allocation prevents performance throttling typical of burstable tiers, but overall throughput remains constrained by execution speed and memory limits. The instance is suited for lightweight web serving, small microservices, low-volume background workers, and development environments.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon architecture. It provides 1 dedicated vCPU operating at 2.3 GHz along with 3.75 GB of RAM, reflecting a balanced entry-level compute-to-memory profile. The instance includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 45 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES, and BMI2 instruction sets. It features no bundled local storage and no included public IPv4 addresses, relying on external disk configurations for persistent data. Synthetic testing places performance in the entry bracket, achieving 895.0 in Geekbench single-core, 1088.79 in stress-ng, and 1.29 million Redis SET operations per second. Static web serving reaches 1.21 GB/sec. This configuration is best suited for low-demand applications, lightweight API gateways, and non-critical development services.
